name: sudoku
title: Sudoku
description: Sudoku in the panel, made on your machine: a daily puzzle for each of Easy, Medium, Hard and Expert (the same for everyone on that day) and a new one whenever you like, graded by the techniques it takes, not the clue count. Notes without an extra step (a second digit in a cell turns it into notes), auto notes that keep every cell's options for you, a digit-first mode; hints that say where to look, then why, in plain words; undo, a clock, streaks and times per difficulty. Every move is saved, so Escape anywhere loses nothing.
author: pal

settings.label: Opens on
settings.description: Whose daily the first open shows when nothing is left half-done. ⌘N picks any difficulty either way.

settings.label: Checking
settings.description: Clashes are the same digit twice in a row, column or box. Mistakes also mark a digit that is not the answer, and count them. Also on ⌘K.

options.title: Show mistakes as you make them

settings.label: Clock
settings.text: Show the time while you play
settings.description: Off hides the running time. Your times still count for stats and show when you finish. Also T or ⌘K in the game.

settings.label: Auto notes
settings.text: Keep every empty cell's notes filled in for me
settings.description: Each empty cell shows the digits that still fit, updated as you play; you only take out the ones you rule out, and they stay out. Off brings your own notes back. Also C or ⌘K in the game.

store.tagline: Daily sudoku in four difficulties, notes without an extra step, hints that explain
features: A daily puzzle per difficulty, the same on every machine that day, and a new one of any difficulty on ⌘N; nothing is fetched
Graded by how a person solves it: Easy takes only singles you can spot, Medium a cell with one digit left, Hard pairs and locked candidates, Expert X-wings, swordfish and XY-wings
Notes without an extra step: type a different digit over one you placed and the cell turns into notes holding both; Backspace clears it
Auto notes (C, a setting): every empty cell shows the digits that still fit, updated as you play; you only take out the ones you rule out, and they stay out
Digit first (D): pick a digit, every cell it can still go in lights up, and each click places it
A pad of slim keys: a click places, a right-click, ⌥-click or the key's corner writes the note; a bar under each digit for how many are down, a check once all nine are
Notes in a 3 by 3 inside the cell, also Shift or Option with a digit or N for notes mode; a placed digit clears itself from the notes it sees; A fills every note in, Shift-A clears them
Clues solid, your digits in the accent colour; the cursor's row, column and box lit, every copy of its digit lit, that digit's notes circled across the board
A clash is a red line under your digit with the clue it runs into ringed; every mistake in red as you make it if you want (a setting)
Hints in three presses: where to look, then why in plain words ("Only this cell in row 4 can take a 7"), then the move; the cells that explain it are circled
Undo and redo, erase, Tab to the next empty cell, arrows or H J K L, one row of tools, a line filling as the cells do
A sweep of light when a row, column or box is done, a ripple and confetti for the board
A clock that runs only while the board is on screen, and a pause that hides it; T hides the clock if it rushes you (times still count)
Browse every daily by month and every half-done game; stats per difficulty: best and average time, the streak, a chart, the history
